diagram_classification: cosmological / natural-philosophical (macrocosm diagram combining the four elements, qualities, seasons, cardinal directions and the three continents in a T-O-like map scheme)
interpretation: The diagram is a schematic of cosmic order that correlates the four elements (ignis, aer, aqua, terra) with their paired qualities (calidus, siccus, humidus, frigidus), the four seasons (ver, aestas, autumnus, hiems) and the four cardinal directions (Oriens, Auster, Occidens, Aquilo). A rotated square (rhombus) with a circle at each vertex is set inside a larger framing square. The directions sit in the vertex circles and the seasons on the connecting bands. Each season band lies between two directions and names the two qualities it combines: spring is hot and moist (ver calidum et humidum), summer is hot and dry (aestas calida sicca), autumn is dry and cold (autumnus siccus frigidus) and winter is cold and moist (hiems frigidus humidus). Each element sits in a corner of the outer square with its qualities: fire is hot and dry, air is hot and moist, water is cold and moist, earth is cold and dry. The interior is divided by a vertical and a horizontal line into the three known continents, Asia (upper left), Africa (upper right) and Europa (the whole lower half), which recalls the T-O map layout. The diagram thus presents the world as a microcosm-macrocosm system in which geography, time, the elements and the humoral qualities are linked. The directions are given in an unconventional orientation: Auster (south) is at the top, Oriens (east) at the left, Occidens (west) at the right and Aquilo (north) at the bottom.
evidence: Visible and written in the diagram: the labels IGNIS, AER, AQUA, TERRA; the quality labels CALIDUS, SICCUS, HUMIDUS, FRIGIDA; the band inscriptions VER CALIDUM ET HUMIDUM, AESTAS CALIDA SICCA, AUTUMNUS SICCUS FRIGIDUS and HIEMS FRIGIDUS HUMIDUS; the direction names AUSTER, ORIENS, OCCIDENS, AQUILO; and the continent names ASIA, AFRICA, EUROPA divided by the cross lines. External knowledge: this is the standard early medieval scheme of elements, qualities, seasons and winds, found in Isidorean-type natural-philosophical and computistical compilations, and the tripartite continent layout resembles T-O maps. The reading of the colour coding (dark red for fire, pale for air, green for water, dark grey for earth) and the assignment of the continents to the cardinal axes is more tentative.
